input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: the wrapper now clears and reuses one statistics dict for every call instead of giving each call its own, so concurrent or nested calls of the same decorated function write into the same dict
- failure path: two threads (or two concurrent awaits of the async wrapper) call the same decorated function; the second call's stats.clear() wipes the first call's start_time and attempt_number, and both read a merged, wrong statistics view afterwards

Reviewer finding
- description: The wrapper now clears and reuses one shared statistics dict on every call to the decorated function. Concurrent or nested/recursive calls of the same wrapped function therefore share and mutate the same dict.
- rationale: Trigger: the same decorated function runs in two threads, or recursively. The second call's stats.clear() wipes the first call's in-progress counters, and both calls then write into the same dict. Impact: attempt_number, idle_for and the other statistics are corrupted. The old code created a fresh dict per call via copy.statistics, and the comment above this hunk says the copy exists to avoid exactly this overwriting.
critique: The finding describes the same mechanism as the label: the wrapper reuses one shared statistics dict and clears it on each call. As a result, concurrent or nested calls of the same function wipe and overwrite each other's statistics.
